evidence_notes: Kambi Group plc (Malta-incorporated, KAMBI on Nasdaq Stockholm First North Premier) is a pure B2B sportsbook technology/trading supplier, spun out of Unibet's sportsbook operation (est. 2010, IPO 2014). Q2 2026 revenue EUR45.9m (+13.5% YoY) on World Cup turnover; FY26 EBITA guidance raised to EUR23-27m. Reported 48% of network bets AI-traded in 2025, rising to 60% by Q1 2026, with a stated goal of 100% AI-traded pricing/risk for the 2026 World Cup. New partnerships in 2026: PMU (France market entry), Atlantic/BC Lottery and Canadian Bank Note (Americas), ComeOn Group (data/personalisation), plus extensions with BetWarrior, Desert Diamond, Paf. Market cap ~SEK4.77bn as of Jul 2026 (stockanalysis.com), converted to ~USD470m at an approximate rate — not independently verified. Headcount, exact licence list, debt/leverage and RG stance were not confirmed within the research budget and are left null rather than guessed.
notes: Resolved to the listed parent Kambi Group plc, not any operator brand (Kambi has no B2C brand). No subsidiary/duplicate risk identified against other igaming batch entries. Scored consistently against Evolution AB (Dormant, invisible-to-player B2B supplier archetype) and Sportradar (Sleeping giant, B2B data/AI leader) anchors: Kambi's distribution readiness (proven platform + broad regulated reach) sits near Sportradar's level, its AI readiness is elevated by genuinely unusual, well-evidenced AI-trading automation, but willingness stays low like Evolution because Kambi's business model is built on empowering operators, not bypassing them.
